full_text:
There are multiple tools and strategies a fantasy drafter, beginner or experienced, can and should go into a draft with. We’ve provided you with every angle for multiple league types and setups, but when you get down to it, fantasy is a simple game: __draft the right players__. Even Jimmy Johnson, who wheeled-and-dealed the Cowboys to three Super Bowl titles in the early '90s, said that was his big “secret.”

It’s a lot easier said than done, but let’s examine our methodology for doing just that.

A __“VALUE”__ is a player who is likely to outperform his ADP, and those players are useful when building a roster. These players are often overlooked in drafts because they lack the upside to be true game-changing players on a championship roster. They’re very appealing at their cost, though.

A __“TARGET”__ is, essentially, a player the market has read correctly. This player is priced fairly but provides enough equity at ADP that drafters should not go bargain-hunting — you need to pay market value to get their championship-level production on your team. “Targets” are players who provide the meat-and-potatoes foundation for your roster.

A __“____LEAGUE-WINNER____”__ is the select few players we’ve identified who provide the championship-level production you need to take bragging rights. In a day when the fantasy community is sharper than ever, these are the least common of the three categories. A “league-winner” has more in common with a “target” than with a “value” — “league-winners” are players for whom we will occasionally go *above* market value to secure.

A good Fantasy Points-endorsed roster will have a mix of these players. We’re more willing to pay at or above market value for an outstanding player than to try to go bargain-hunting constantly. But securing those values at the right time — especially if the player has massive upside — is what’ll get you across the finish line.

This article is broken down by position and sorted by ADP. Based on that ADP, our projections, and any news and notes that have come out, we'll let you know if that player is a value, target, or league-winner.

\>This article will be constantly updated leading up to the start of the season. The ADP in this article is based on our [ADP tool’s PPR setting](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/rankings/adp#/), which pulls from PPR Sleeper drafts over the last 14 days…We don’t list the most obvious players at the very top of drafts.

 

{{CTA|FFPC|omit=\[none\]}}

__Quarterbacks__
----------------

#### VALUE: __{{Jalen Hurts|QB|PHI|21831}}__ (Phi)

\>ADP 67 QB6, PROJ QB4

Hurts is coming off the worst fantasy season under one-done playcaller __Kevin Patullo__, but he still finished as the QB7 with 19.3 FPG. He’s going off the board in that range this summer, but he lived in the top six at the position in his first four seasons as a full-time starter. He never dipped below 21.7 FPG from 2021-24, which included a pair of runner-up finishes to __Josh Allen__ in 2022-23. Hurts has a new playcaller for the 11th straight season since he enrolled at Alabama for the 2016 season. They went outside the organization to hire __Sean Mannion__ to take over Patullo, who was an internal hire. Patullo sank Philly’s offense to 17th in EPA (13.0) and 21st in points/drive (2.03) last season after they ranked sixth in EPA (112.4) and fifth in points/drive (2.72) under outside hire __Kellen Moore__ in 2024. Mannion comes from a __Sean McVay__\-__Matt LaFleur__ background, and his new scheme will include more under-center plays, including play-action from under center.

[Per Ryan Heath](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/new-playcallers-fantasy-football-impact#/), 92.7% of Hurts’ dropbacks have come from the shotgun over the past five seasons, while Mannion and the Packers had __Jordan Love__ drop back from under center at the ninth-highest rate (24.8%) last season. Like most QBs, Hurts has been significantly better in YPA (8.76>7.44), FP/DB (.56>.47), and CPOE (7%>3.5%) from under center than in shotgun since 2021. Hurts must run more in his age-28 season, and Mannion said this spring that Hurts’ legs will be a part of his wide-zone running scheme. Scott DiBenedetto is expecting Philadelphia’s O-line to [bounce back](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/nfl-offensive-line-rankings#/) from an injury-riddled campaign, which should benefit Hurts, who posted career-lows in rushing attempts (6.6) and rushing YPG (26.3). We’re optimistic Hurts can get back on track at a much cheaper ADP under his new playcaller, and the loss of __A.J. Brown__ could be an addition by subtraction for Hurts’ fantasy production.

#### VALUE: __{{Dak Prescott|QB|DAL|18055}}__ (Dal)

\>ADP 90 QB10, PROJ QB7

Prescott and the Cowboys are the NFC version of __Joe Burrow__ and the Bengals, but Prescott can be selected multiple rounds after Burrow goes off the board. Dak threw just 11 TDs in eight games with __Brandin Cooks__ as his #2 WR in 2024, but he turned things around with 30 TDs last season with __George Pickens__ teaming up with __CeeDee Lamb__ at WR. Prescott is coming off a QB7 finish (20.3) if you toss out Week 18 when he played one half, and he led all passers in attempts/game (36.8), completions/game (24.8), and passing YPG (280.1) in that same span.

Prescott ranks third in completions/game (23.9), second in TD passes/game (1.96), and first in end-zone targets/game (2.73) since returning from his catastrophic leg injury during the 2020 season. Prescott finished behind only __Matthew Stafford__ with 50 end-zone attempts, and the Cowboys are expected to score plenty of touchdowns after scoring the fifth-most points/drive (2.63). Dallas’ defense may improve some, but it is still expected to play in plenty of shootouts with the fourth-highest [implied team total](https://x.com/ConnorAllenNFL/status/2057527213222727779?s=20) (25.68) based on Vegas lines for the upcoming season. Prescott is averaging just 11.4 rushing YPG since his leg injury, so he’s unlikely to challenge for the most FPG at the position. He’s still a value at his ADP with QB11 finishes or better in total FP in his seven healthy seasons in 10 years.

#### TARGET: __{{Trevor Lawrence|QB|JAX|22490}}__ (Jax)

\>ADP 92 QB, PROJ QB8

Lawrence’s career has been littered with times when it looked like he turned a corner, only for him to come crashing back to earth. This season could be different because he’s in the best situation he’s ever been in entering his second campaign under __Liam Coen__. He coaxed career highs in touchdown passes from Lawrence (29) and __Baker Mayfield__ (41) in back-to-back seasons. Lawrence’s season took off after the Jaguars acquired __Jakobi Meyers__ before Week 10, which aligned with __Parker Washington__ jumping into __Travis Hunter__’s old role. Lawrence posted 13 total TDs and 17.5 FPG (QB17) in his first eight games before turning in 20 total TDs and 23.7 FPG (QB1) in his final nine games. He won plenty of fantasy championships in Weeks 15-17, finishing as the QB1 with 33.2 FPG in the fantasy playoffs.

Lawrence has reached 560+ attempts in each of his four healthy seasons, and the Jaguars ranked seventh in pass rate over expectation (4.3%) in their first season under Coen. He posted the sixth-most end-zone attempts (38) last season and ranks fourth in EZ attempts/game (2.52) over the last four years. Jacksonville figures to remain pass-heavy with an inexperienced backfield behind Lawrence after letting __Travis Etienne__ walk in free agency. Lawrence’s rushing production will regress after posting career-highs in yards (359), TDs (9), and FPG (5.3), but he has some untapped potential if he can get on the same page with __Brian Thomas__. He actually had the second-largest difference (-2.0) in FPG and expected FPG, largely due to his missed connections with BTJ. Lawrence is equipped to post another strong season, and a potentially elite fantasy finish as he enters the prime of his career with the best receiving corps and coaching of his career.

{{PAYWALL}}

#### TARGET: __{{Brock Purdy|QB|SF|23241}}__ (SF)

\>ADP 104 QB13, PROJ QB10

Purdy missed eight games for a severe turf toe injury last season, but he was a fantasy difference-maker and a league-winner when he was on the field. He finished as the QB5 with 21.0 FPG, including 32.3 FPG (QB2) in the fantasy playoffs in Weeks 15-17. Purdy is in a better position heading into his fifth season after the 49ers landed him __Mike Evans__ in free agency. Purdy lacked a true perimeter and downfield threat, which was exposed in a pair of dismal performances against a Seattle defense that took away the middle of the field at the end of last season. Evans is one of the premier touchdown scorers of his generation, ranking 10th all-time and behind only __Davante Adams__ among active players with 108 TD receptions. Purdy already owns an elite 6.2% TD rate through four seasons, which ranks behind only __Lamar Jackson__ (6.5%) among active QBs.

The 49ers ranked sixth in PROE from inside the 10-yard line (5.7%) last season without Evans in the mix, and Purdy tied for fifth with 2.44 end-zone attempts per game. San Francisco’s schedule isn’t as easy as last season’s slate, but they’ll still face the NFL’s sixth-easiest schedule based on win totals. That’s reflected in the 49ers having the seventh-highest [implied team total](https://x.com/ConnorAllenNFL/status/2057527213222727779/photo/1) based on Vegas lines for the upcoming season. Purdy added scrambling to his arsenal to defeat defenses, averaging 2.58 scrambles/game and 19.6 rushing YPG with 8 rushing TDs in 24 starts the last two seasons. He started his career averaging .92 scrambles/game and 9.1 rushing YPG with 3 rushing TDs in his first 24 starts. He should remain active as a scrambler, especially if he’s back to full health off his turf toe injury. Purdy hasn’t finished lower than the QB10 in his three seasons as a full-time starter, and he has league-winning upside as he showed in the fantasy playoffs.

#### VALUE: __{{Malik Willis|QB|MIA|23118}}__ (Mia)

\>ADP 138 QB18, PROJ QB16

Willis landed a big payday from the Dolphins — $45 million guaranteed — despite starting just three games over the last two seasons. He received some hype as a potential first-round prospect before the 2022 draft, but he slipped to Tennessee at 86th overall. The Titans didn’t really give him much of a chance to play in two seasons, and they cleared the way for __Will Levis__ to play by sending Willis to the Packers for just a seventh-round pick before the 2024 season. Willis surprised the league by playing well in relief of __Jordan Love__ early in the 2024 season, keeping the Packers on track with a pair of victories while averaging .75 FP/DB.

He was then the best fantasy quarterback when he was on the field last season, scoring 52.2 FP on just 47 dropbacks for an incredible 1.11 FP/DB. For perspective, __Josh Allen__ averaged .54 FP/DB on his way to finishing as the QB1. Willis is a true dual-threat who instantly became a mid-QB2 by landing a starting job, even in a potentially bad offense that didn’t do him any favors by trading __Jaylen Waddle__ to the Broncos. Willis is the type of quarterback who hurts the fantasy outlooks for his skill players since he’ll steal production with his rushing ability. Miami’s dearth of offensive talent gives Willis an ugly floor, but he’s still worth a flier because he has top-12 upside if he continues to run a lot and if Miami’s defense forces him to play in some high-scoring games.

#### VALUE: __{{Kyler Murray|QB|MIN|20889}}__ (Min)

\>ADP 142 QB20, PROJ QB19

The Vikings are calling it an open competition between Murray and __J.J. McCarthy__ in training camp, but Murray will have to fall flat on his face to lose the Week 1 starting job to Nine. The franchise signed Murray to give this offense a lift after McCarthy averaged 163.2 passing YPG with more INTs (12) than TDs (11), whose struggles visibly frustrated star WR __Justin Jefferson__. __Kevin O’Connell__ had a strong record of getting the best out of his quarterbacks until McCarthy flopped last year. O’Connell’s offenses ranked in the top six in passing yards and pass rate over expectation in each of his first three seasons as head coach before last year’s quarterback situation undermined the entire offense.

He could get back to his pass-happy ways with a competent triggerman. Murray wants to get his career back on track like __Sam Darnold__ did before winning the Super Bowl with Seattle in his first season away from Minnesota. He averaged 7.9 YPA, 254.1 passing YPG, and 19.1 FPG to finish as the QB9 during his only season under O’Connell. Murray isn’t guaranteed to start all season, especially if he plays like he did last season, but he’ll be a high-end QB2 option with top-five upside when he’s in the lineup because of his career 36.7 rushing YPG average.

#### TARGET: __{{Tyler Shough|QB|NO|23187}}__ (NO)

\>ADP 144 QB21, PROJ QB17

Shough couldn’t crack the starting lineup to start his rookie season, but he eventually showed real potential as a 26-year-old rookie once he took over for __Spencer Rattler__ in Week 8. He reached 17.1+ FP and 239+ passing yards in seven of his final eight starts despite a weak receiving corps behind __Chris Olave__, ranking as the QB9 (18.8) from Week 10 through the end of the season. He looks like a big, stiff QB (6’5”, 219), but he averaged 19.7 rushing YPG with 3 rushing TDs in his starts. New Orleans needed to determine if Shough is the quarterback of the future, and they selected __Jordyn Tyson__ eighth overall to get a proper evaluation. Tyson was one of the late risers in the draft process despite concerns about durability and effort. Brett Whitefield saw shades of __CeeDee Lamb__ in Tyson’s play style, and he’ll immediately slot in next to Olave.

Shough’s supporting cast is sneaky strong after inking __Travis Etienne__ to a big deal. __Juwan Johnson__ is coming off a career year at 29 years old, and __Devaughn Vele__ rounds out a strong receiving corps after playing well in his final month of action. Shough could take a major step forward in __Kellen Moore__’s fantasy-friendly offense, which played at the NFL’s fastest pace last season. They averaged a play every 26.6 seconds, which led to the 11th-most plays/game (63.2). Moore’s up-tempo offenses helped __Jalen Hurts__ (QB5), __Justin Herbert__ (QB12), and __Dak Prescott__ (QB13) to finish as top-13 options in three straight seasons from 2022-24. Shough showed that kind of upside once he got his bearings after his first two starts, but he’s going off the board as a low-end QB2.

__Running Backs__
-----------------

#### TARGET: __{{Saquon Barkley|RB|PHI}}__ (Phi)

\>ADP 20 RB10, PROJ RB5

We don’t typically feature top-24 picks in this article, but Barkley stands out as a strong pick with his late second-round ADP on some drafting platforms. Saquon is looking to get back among the league leaders in his third season with the Eagles. He led the NFL in attempts (345), rushing yards (2005), and FPG (22.3) in his first season in Philadelphia, before dipping to 1140 rushing yards and 14.6 FPG (RB15) last year. The Eagles canned __Kevin Patullo__ after one disastrous season, after elevating him following __Kellen Moore__’s departure for New Orleans. Philly ranked 18th in EPA/rush (-.070), 14th in rushing TDs (17), and 15th in rate of drives ending in touchdowns (24.2%) under Patullo after ranking second in EPA/rush (.036), second in rushing TDs (29), and seventh in rate of drives ending in touchdowns (28.7%) during their Super Bowl-winning campaign. The Eagles are undergoing massive offensive changes under __Sean Mannion__, who comes from a __Sean McVay__\-__Matt LaFleur__ background.

Barkley [said the new system](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7314956/2026/05/29/saquon-barkley-eagles-offense-system-otas/) will include the most under-center and outside zone concepts he’s had in his career. Barkley said under-center runs help him see the field better and run downhill quicker. Saquon averaged 3.09 YBC/ATT and 4.92 YPC with a 15% explosive run rate on 108 under-center runs last season, compared to 1.50 YBC/ATT and 3.54 YPC with an 8.2% explosive run rate on 172 shotgun runs. A healthier offensive line would certainly help Barkley to return to his 2024 form, and the group checked in as the fifth-best line in Scott DeBenedetto’s [Offensive Line Rankings](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/nfl-offensive-line-rankings#/). Barkley was bound to regress off his monster 2024 campaign, but the pendulum swung too far in the other direction. Barkley will push for elite production with better play-calling and a healthier offensive line.

#### VALUE: __{{Breece Hall|RB|NYJ|22526}}__ (NYJ)

\>ADP 32 RB17, PROJ RB13

The Jets slapped the franchise tag on Hall in March before giving him a three-year extension and $29 million guaranteed two months later. Hall averaged 4.5 YPC, 90.0 scrimmage YPG, 3.4 receptions/game and 15.3 FPG to start his career, even while tearing his ACL seven games into his rookie campaign. He reached 1359+ scrimmage yards in each of the last three seasons, but he hasn’t scored more than 5 rushing TDs in any season playing in Jets offenses that have finished in the bottom nine in total offense and scoring offense every year since he arrived in 2022. Hall ranked ninth in first-down runs (57) and fourth in rate of 15+ yard runs (7%) among 49 RBs who had 100+ carries last season.

It would’ve been fun to see Hall in another offense if he made it to free agency, but he should see bell-cow usage once again in New York, which gives him top-12 potential. __Braelon Allen__ is coming off an MCL injury, but he was sitting at just a 17% carry share and a 28% snap share through the first three weeks before his injury in Week 4. New York’s offensive line has some upside if first-round picks __Armand Membou__ and __Olu Fashanu__ take steps forward. __Geno Smith__ should also raise the floor for this offense after the Jets ranked last in YPA (5.64) and 28th in EPA/play (-.15) with __Justin Fields__, __Tyrod Taylor__, and __Brady Cook__ running the show. New York should be more efficient finding the end zone after scoring TDs on just 14.4% of their drives (29th), which will help Breece push for a top-12 finish.

#### LEAGUE-WINNER: __{{Cam Skattebo|RB|NYG|25887}}__ (NYG)

\>ADP 21 RB49, PROJ RB17

Skattebo [botched](https://x.com/UnderdogNFL/status/2078888031226876050?s=20) his trademark backflip at an event just before training camp, but he still proved his point: his leg is healthy, and he’s ready to play. At the start of the season, he’ll be more than 10 months removed from the right ankle dislocation, fibula fracture, and deltoid ligament rupture that prematurely ended his excellent rookie season. He quickly climbed to the top of New York’s depth chart last season, ahead of __Tyrone Tracy__ and __Devin Singletary__. He reached 13+ FP in six consecutive games and 90+ scrimmage yards in five straight games before his injury. Skattebo averaged 16.0/66.8/.8 rushing and 3.5/29.5/.2 receiving per game in the six games he played more than half of the snaps, averaging a healthy 18.6 FPG, which would’ve made him the RB6 over the whole season.

He posted a 64% snap share, a 51% carry share, and 49% route share in Weeks 2-7 before suffering his injury early in Week 8. Players returning from similar injuries have been fantasy potholes in the recent past (e.g., __Isiah Pacheco__ and __Tony Pollard__), but it’s encouraging that the Giants passed on adding to the backfield in free agency and the draft. He’ll need to prove he’s healthy enough to warrant another large workload in training camp, but he has a chance to replicate his success from his rookie season in a better offensive environment if __Malik Nabers__ is healthy too. Skattebo has a lower floor than most of the backs being selected around him if his leg injury proves difficult to bounce back from, but he also proved as a rookie to have a higher ceiling than the backs being drafted around him.

#### VALUE: __{{David Montgomery|RB|HOU|20882}}__ (Hou)

\>ADP 56 RB23, PROJ RB19

Montgomery requested a trade after his opportunities dipped once __Dan Campbell__ took over playcalling in Week 10. Detroit granted his wish by sending him to Houston for __Juice Scruggs__, a 2026 fourth-round pick, and a 2027 seventh-round pick, and the Texans immediately locked him into a two-year deal that included $10 million guaranteed. Houston has big plans for its new lead back after __Joe Mixon__’s season-long absence forced __Woody Marks__ into a role he wasn’t ready to handle. Monty is Houston’s latest hired hand at the position, following in Mixon’s path from the 2024 season. Mixon, at 28 years old, ranked as the RB10 with 17.2 FPG in his only season as Houston’s lead back, averaging 17.5 carries and 2.6 receptions per game.

Monty averaged 4.2 YPC or better in each of his three seasons for the Lions, including a strong 4.53 YPC last season when he ranked 12th in YACO/ATT (2.45). Montgomery reached 34+ receptions, 301+ receiving yards, and at least a 65% snap share in each of his final three seasons as the lead back for the Bears in 2020-22. Houston’s offensive line needed a significant upgrade after ranking 30th in adjusted YBC/ATT (1.45) and 30th in success rate (45.1%) last season. The Texans beefed up their offensive line by selecting __Keylan Rutledge__ at No. 26, which came after they acquired __Braden Smith__ and __Wyatt Teller__ earlier this offseason. Monty is a safe bet to post RB2 production based on volume alone, and he’s shown a nose for the end zone by averaging 9 TDs per season. He has top-12 upside as Mixon showed two years ago if Houston scores on more than 17.6% of its drives (27th) as they did last season.

#### LEAGUE-WINNER: __{{Bhaysul Tuten|RB|JAX}}__ (Jax)

\>ADP 60 RB24, PROJ RB23

Tuten has a wider range of outcomes than most backs being selected inside the top 24 at the position, including potentially elite upside if he clearly becomes the lead option in one of the NFL’s better offenses. The second-year RB will get the first crack to replace __Travis Etienne__, who finished as the RB14 with 14.9 FPG before signing with the Saints this offseason. [Per Ryan Heath](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/heaths-favorite-best-ball-values#/), __Liam Coen__ ranks third among all playcallers in EPA/play (0.15), seventh in yards per play (6.31), and first in PPG (28.7) since 2021. The Jaguars brought in __Chris Rodriguez__ to be Tuten’s primary competition for touches after the Commanders decided not to tender the restricted free agent. C-Rod needed surgery on his left foot in the spring, which gave Tuten a runway to grab the lead role in spring practices.

Tuten mustered just 83/307/5 rushing and 10/79/3 receiving as a change-of-pace option behind Etienne. He finished with [the h](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2057062758676312239?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2057062758676312239%7Ctwgr%5E50f5a94bd24060519ae5d8d3ec3213b5fd4e9a88%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fantasypoints.com%2Fnfl%2Farticles%2Fseason%2F2026%2Fheaths-favorite-best-ball-values)[ighest success rate](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2057062758676312239?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2057062758676312239%7Ctwgr%5E50f5a94bd24060519ae5d8d3ec3213b5fd4e9a88%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fantasypoints.com%2Fnfl%2Farticles%2Fseason%2F2026%2Fheaths-favorite-best-ball-values) (57.8%) among rookie RBs since 2021, largely because of his short-yardage success — 17 of his 83 carries (20.4%) came from 2 yards to go. He converted 12 of those carries into first downs/touchdowns, but it also hurt his overall efficiency. Tuten averaged 2.40 YACO/ATT and excelled in short-yardage situations, and he’ll get to show off his 4.28 speed in longer down-and-distance situations this season. He also bested pass-pro back __LeQuint Allen__ as a receiver despite far fewer opportunities as rookies. Allen ran 68 more routes than Tuten (143>75), but Tuten commanded more targets (13>11) and posted more receiving yards (79>54) than his fellow second-year back. Tuten could easily pay off his ADP if he ends up being the lead back in a three-man committee in one of the NFL’s best offenses. And he has league-winning upside if he relegates Rodriguez to a limited role and loses minimal pass-catching opportunities to Allen.

#### VALUE: __{{D’Andre Swift|RB|CHI|17124}}__ (Chi)

\>ADP 65 RB25, PROJ RB22

Swift is one of the safest bets to finish as an RB2 because that’s just what the guy has done almost every single season since he broke into the league in 2020. He’s never finished higher than RB10 in 2021 and never lower than RB25 in 2023, and last season was no different under first-time head coach __Ben Johnson__. He finished as the RB16 by clearing 1300+ scrimmage yards for the second straight season since joining the Bears, even with seventh-round __Kyle Monangai__ emerging to make this backfield a two-man committee. Swift reached 71+ scrimmage yards in 12 of his final 14 games (postseason included) after Chicago’s Week 5 bye, which powered him to career-highs in rushing yards (1087) and TDs (10).

He finished 10th in YPC (4.87), fifth in explosive run rate (15.1%), eighth in YBC/ATT (2.69), and third in EPA/attempt (.07) in his second go-round with Johnson as his playcaller. He should continue to have success before contact running behind Scott DiBenedetto’s [third-ranked offensive line](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/nfl-offensive-line-rankings#/) and with Johnson calling plays. Swift has a solid floor as an RB2 if he continues to hold off Monangai to be Chicago’s top back. And he has bell-cow potential if Monangai misses time, with just __Roschon Johnson__ and his 2 carries from last season currently third on the depth chart.

#### VALUE: __{{Rhamondre Stevenson|RB|NE|22546}}__ (NE)

\>ADP 83 RB30, PROJ RB24

__Mike Vrabel__ and __Josh McDaniels__ told us who they trusted the most in the Patriots backfield when it was nut-cutting time in the postseason. New England selected the explosive __TreVeyon Henderson__ 38th overall before the 2025 season, but the coaching staff leaned on Stevenson during their four-game playoff run. Stevenson paced Henderson in snap share (70%>31%), scrimmage yards (343>109), receptions (12>5), and FPG (13.1>4.0) during New England’s run to the Super Bowl. Henderson is the more intriguing prospect entering his second season, but Stevenson is a proven entity entering his sixth season with an ADP that is three rounds cheaper.

Stevenson bettered Henderson in just about every key rushing metric during the regular season, including explosive run rate (13%>11.1%), YAC/ATT (2.75>1.91), and MTF/ATT (.23>.13). He was also better in key receiving metrics like YPRR (1.41>.98), 1D/RR (.045>.031) and route share (48.8%>36.7%), and perhaps most importantly, McDaniels trusted him more in pass protection. He also bested him in FPG (13.0>12.2) for a RB22 finish. Stevenson will have to take a significant step back, or Henderson will have to take a significant step forward for their roles to flip in 2026, which is certainly possible given Henderson’s pedigree. We’d rather not pay a fourth-round price to find out, and we’ll take the discounted Stevenson as our RB3 at a much cheaper ADP.

#### TARGET: __{{Kenneth Gainwell|RB|TB|22562}}__ (TB)

\>ADP 107 RB36, PROJ RB31

Pittsburgh got a lot of bang for its buck with Gainwell on a one-year, $1.79 million deal last season. His price significantly went up in his second trip to free agency, earning $9.8 million guaranteed to challenge __Bucky Irving__ for touches. The Buccaneers could’ve brought __Rachaad White__ on a much cheaper deal — he settled for $1.7 million guaranteed from the Commanders — but they viewed Gainwell as an upgrade for this backfield. He quickly earned the trust of __Aaron Rodgers__, becoming the #2 option in the passing game behind __D.K. Metcalf__. #### LEAGUE-WINNER: __{{Tyler Warren|TE|IND|25874}}__ (Ind)

\>ADP 50 TE4, PROJ TE3

Warren will take on a bigger role in the passing game after the Colts decided to pay __Alec Pierce__ and trade away __Michael Pittman__ to the Steelers. Warren finished second in target share (19.4%) and first-read share (22.2%) for the Colts as a rookie, and Pittman left behind team-highs in target share (19.7%) and first-read share (23.2%). He finished as the TE11 with 11.1 FPG, but he failed to reach double-digit FP in his final five games, which corresponded with __Daniel Jones__ rupturing his Achilles. He ranked as the TE7 (13.1) through his first 12 games while Danny Dimes was in the lineup, who is trending toward being ready for the start of the season after being fully cleared for the start of training camp.

Warren was checking out his [A.S.S.](https://data-suite-cwecht.fly.dev/receiving/separation-by-alignment?positions=TE&sortBy=sep_score&qual_routes=200) this offseason after finishing as one of the worst separators at the position — he ranked 37th out of 40 TEs in our Average Separation Score metric (-.025). He wants to be more explosive in his second season, specifically when he’s changing directions. Warren [told ESPN](https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/48968602/colts-tyler-warren-seeks-more-explosiveness-second-season), “A big thing \[is\] the explosion out of my breaks. Getting in the break is one thing, but being able to accelerate out of it and still you create the space, but being able to hold that space if you are running across the field.” He showed plenty of explosiveness when he had the ball in his hands, ranking fourth in YAC/REC (6.50) and second in YAC (494) behind only __Trey McBride__. He actually ranked as the TE5 in expected FPG (11.7), which was the second largest difference (-.6) in FPG and expected FPG behind __T.J. Hockenson__. Warren has room for growth and is a positive regression candidate, which makes him a player to bet on in his second season.

#### TARGET: __{{Tucker Kraft|TE|GB|24118}}__ (GB)

\>ADP 67 TE6, PROJ TE12

Kraft carried Green Bay’s passing game through the first seven games before a torn ACL ended his season prematurely. The injury cut short a potential league-winning season in his third year. He was tied with __Trey McBride__ as the TE1 with 16.2 FPG through the first eight weeks, and he led all receivers in YAC/REC (10.66). Kraft tore his ACL in Week 9, and it appears he’s well on his way to being close to 100% for the start of the season. He told reporters on June 10 that he expects to play in Week 1 without a snap count, but he anticipates starting training camp on the PUP list. He certainly benefited from __Christian Watson__ sitting out the first six games of last season and __Jayden Reed__ breaking his collarbone in Week 2, but __Matt LaFleur__ should be motivated to keep Kraft heavily involved after his Year 3 breakout. The Packers put their trust in their current receivers by thinning out their WR corps, letting __Romeo Doubs__ walk, and trading __Dontayvion Wicks__.

Kraft ranked 20th at the position with j 24.7 routes/game in his healthy contests, which has the chance to improve this season if he’s healthy. Green Bay could tighten its receiver rotations, which could result in an uptick in pace of play after ranking 27th (30.0 seconds/play) the last two seasons. The Packers could also throw it more with __Josh Jacobs__’ legal situation hanging over the offense after ranking 30th in pass rate over expectation (-3.4%) and pass attempts (968) over Jacobs’ first two seasons. Kraft ran white hot before his injury last season, and he has elite upside if he sees a bump in his routes and targets heading into his fourth season.

#### TARGET: __{{Dallas Goedert|TE|PHI|19863}}__ (Phi)

\>ADP 109 TE15, PROJ TE9

Goedert continues to be an underrated fantasy asset despite coming off career-highs in receptions (60), receiving TDs (11), and FPG (12.3) to finish as the TE6 last season. __DeVonta Smith__ is the biggest winner from the __A.J. Brown__ trade, who is the clear top option for __Jalen Hurts__ for the first time in his career. Goedert is also a massive winner from the June trade, but it’s gone completely under the radar based on his ADP. Goedert averages 5.4 targets/game, 53.4 receiving YPG, and 12.3 FPG in seven games without Brown, compared to 4.2 targets/game, 34.5 receiving YPG, and 8.5 FPG with Brown in the lineup. Goedert should see an uptick in target share (18.1%) and first-read share (21.4%) from the last four seasons, with Brown leaving a 27.5% target share (third) and a 35.6% first-read share (first) from that span.

Smith will run more routes on the perimeter, which should open up more opportunities in the middle of the field for Goedert, who will mostly compete with rookie __Makai Lemon__ for those targets. Hurts should be more active in the middle of the field in __Sean Mannion__’s new offense, which will put a bigger emphasis on under-center and playaction dropbacks. The Eagles drafted __Eli Stowers__ in the second round, who will eventually challenge Goedert for opportunities, but the rookie could be a work-in-progress this season, especially as an in-line blocker. Goedert will certainly face touchdown regression after scoring 11 TDs in 15 games last season. He scored 24 times in his first 93 contests (3.4 per season). Brown’s departure will offset some of Goedert’s TD regression, which gives him a great chance to finish as a top-12 TE for the eighth straight season since taking over __Zach Ertz__ as the lead TE.

#### VALUE: __{{Mark Andrews|TE|BAL|19803}}__ (Bal)

\>ADP 111 TE16, PROJ TE11

Andrews’ career is trending in the wrong direction entering his age-31 season, but he’s been given a golden opportunity to prove he can still play at a high level. He’s coming off career-lows in receiving yards (422) and YPR (8.8) in his eighth season on his way to finishing as the TE24 with 7.7 FPG, but the Ravens clearly believe he still has good football ahead of him. Baltimore’s GM __Eric DeCosta__ handed Andrews a three-year deal with $25.9 million guaranteed last December, despite being in the midst of his down season. DeCosta then let __Isaiah Likely__ walk in free agency for less guaranteed money at the start of free agency before waiting until the 133rd overall pick (__Matthew Hibner__) to select a TE. Baltimore’s series of moves since last December left Andrews as the clear top TE and __Durham Smythe__ as the #2 TE entering the season.

We’re also projecting him to be the #2 receiver behind __Zay Flowers__ in Baltimore’s new-look offense, with __Rashod Bateman__ pushing for targets behind him. The Ravens were one of the most efficient offenses under former OC __Todd Monken__, but they attempted more than 100 fewer passes than the next closest team from 2023-25, averaging just 27.3 attempts/game. Baltimore’s league-low pass rate (53.4%) in that span should regress some under first-year playcaller __Declan Doyle__, who worked under __Ben Johnson__ and __Sean Payton__ the last two years. Baltimore’s offense ranks sixth in [implied team total](https://x.com/ConnorAllenNFL/status/2057527213222727779?s=20) for the season, and he’s finished in the top eight at the position in end-zone targets in every season during the *Fantasy Points Data* era. Andrews has more touchdown upside than most TEs, and he has a path to more consistent targets, which gives him a chance for a bounce-back season.

#### TARGET: __{{Isaiah Likely|TE|NYG|23256}}__ (NYG)

\>ADP 117 TE17, PROJ TE14

Likely followed __John Harbaugh__ to the Giants in free agency, where he’ll get a chance to be the lead tight end ahead of __Theo Johnson__. Likely suffered a foot fracture at the start of training camp in his final season with the Ravens, which forced him to miss the first three games. It may have also contributed to a career-low 21.9 receiving YPG once he returned to the lineup — he wasn’t helped by a down season from __Lamar Jackson__. He’s been used mostly as a receiver to start his career — he finished behind only __Mike Gesicki__ with a 74.9% slot rate among TEs — as he’s yet to top a 60% snap share and a 53% route share in any of his first four seasons. He’ll be just 26 years old this season, and he has some untapped potential after playing behind __Mark Andrews__ to start his career.

Likely notably had his best run as a fantasy asset when Andrews missed time at the end of 2023, ranking as the TE5 in FPG (13.9) in Weeks 12-18. The Ravens ranked fifth in 12 personnel usage (36%) in Harbaugh’s final season in Baltimore, and Likely has a leg up on Johnson for targets and snaps based on his massive deal. He slots in as the #2 receiver for __Jaxson Dart__ behind __Malik Nabers__, who is still on the mend from his ACL and meniscus surgeries from last season. Johnson logged 3+ receptions in 10 of his 12 games as the lead TE with Dart, which came mostly without Nabers on the field. Likely has top-12 potential if he distances himself from secondary receivers like Johnson, __Darnell Mooney__, and __Malachi Fields__, and he has even more upside if Nabers isn’t completely healthy this season.
